subject: Post-demo: Access controls, PII handling & next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@marketsafe.com>, Ben Turner <ben.turner@marketsafe.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Access controls, PII handling & next steps

Hi Claire / Ben —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed set of next steps focused on the access / privacy items you flagged: 

What we saw today
- Platform demo (generation, embeddings, observability).
- Showed token-level cost and per-route dashboards; highlighted model pinning.

Items you asked us to follow up on
1) PII/data residency — can Redwood isolate EU-only data? What residency guarantees and encryption-at-rest options exist?
2) Retention & deletion — default log and KV cache retention, delete-on-request SLA.
3) Support access & RBAC — how support/troubleshooter access is scoped; can we enforce least privilege and have an auditable break-glass flow?
4) Long-term logging — retention window and log export for audits (SIEM ingestion).

What I'm sending now
- redwood-security-summary.pdf (high-level controls, SOC2 status, KMS options)
- breakglass-runbook.md (draft of our break-glass process + approval matrix)

Proposed next steps
- I can set up a 30–45m call with Priyom (solutions) + our Security lead to walk the runbook and RBAC matrix.
- We’ll produce a sample RBAC role matrix and a short MAP for procurement.

Please confirm: 1) Do you want data residency to be strictly EU-only for MarketSafe? 2) Who from procurement should we include on the MAP?

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: redwood-security-summary.pdf, breakglass-runbook.md
From: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@marketsafe.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Turner <ben.turner@marketsafe.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 16:30:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Access controls, PII handling & next steps

Soojin — thanks for the recap and the early docs. A few clarifying Qs from our security & privacy team: 

1) Support access & RBAC
- We need a role-by-role matrix showing which Redwood roles can see raw inputs (full PII) vs. derived outputs. Can you provide a template matrix (CSV preferred)?
- For break-glass: what approvals are required, who logs the justification, and how soon after an emergency can access be revoked? We need the ability to timestamp approvals and export audit trails.

2) Data residency & encryption
- MarketSafe requires EU residency for all customer data. If we go with Redwood Private (VPC), can you confirm the control plane still provides auditability but that customer data never leaves the EU region?
- We prefer customer-managed keys (BYOK). Is that supported in Private deployments?

3) Retention & deletion
- Our policy requires 12 months of immutable audit logs and ability to delete derived caches within 24 hours on request. What are your default retention windows and deletion SLAs?

4) Evidence for procurement
- We will need SOC2 Type II report (latest), a summary of log retention architecture, and a sample SOW with support tiers + breach notification timelines.

Can you share the RBAC matrix and SOW draft ahead of the follow-up call? If possible, include an example of a least-privilege support account and the steps to request temporary elevation.

Thanks,
Claire Nguyen
Head of Security Operations | MarketSafe Financial
claire.nguyen@marketsafe.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@marketsafe.com>, Ben Turner <ben.turner@marketsafe.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:12:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Access controls, PII handling & next steps

Hi Claire / Ben —

Thanks for the detailed questions — I’m Priyom (Solutions Engineering). Short answers and what we’ll include in the pre-read: 

Support access & RBAC
- We’ll attach RBAC_matrix_v1.csv showing roles: Viewer, Analyst, Support-Triage, Support-Limited, Admin. Each role has columns for: raw_input_access, kv_cache_access, ability_to_execute_queries, and session_export capability.
- Break-glass: our runbook requires a two-person approval for elevated support sessions (requestor + on-call security approver). Every session is time-limited (default 2 hours) and logged; revocation is immediate via the control plane and logged to the audit stream. The runbook includes email + ticketing hooks.

Data residency & encryption
- Private (VPC) deployment supports per-region data residency. Control plane endpoints can be routed through customer network; data plane remains in the chosen region. BYOK is supported for Private deployments via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault).

Retention & deletion
- Default platform logs retained 90 days; audit logs for Private can be configured to 12 months (we’ll include options and cost delta). Deletion requests for KV caches and derived artifacts — default SLA 24 hours for Private customers; hosted customers vary (we’ll include the exact SLA options).

Attachments I’m including here for pre-read:
- RBAC_matrix_v1.csv (sample role matrix)
- SOW-draft.pdf (starter SOW with support tiers)
- redwood-security-summary.pdf (SOC2, encryption, logging architecture)

Proposed next step: 45m call with our Security & Solutions team to walk the runbook and RBAC matrix. I can host Friday 19 Jun at 10:00 AM PT. If that works for you we’ll send a calendar invite and add procurement to the MAP.

Owners / contacts from Redwood:
- Soojin Lee — Account Exec (deal owner)
- Priyom Das — Solutions (technical lead)
- Marissa Cole — Customer Success (onboarding & SLOs)
- Security (will join the Friday call)

Regards,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

Attachments: RBAC_matrix_v1.csv, SOW-draft.pdf, redwood-security-summary.pdf
